page: Microsoft Azure E96ds_v6 is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance powered by an Intel Xeon 8573C processor running at up to 4.2 GHz. Configured on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor with x86_64 architecture, the instance provides 96 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 48 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading enabled. The CPU subsystem is supported by 260 MB of L3 cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and 48 KB of L1 data cache per core, alongside instruction set support including AVX-512 and Intel AMX accelerators.

System memory consists of 768.0 GB of RAM, allocating 8.0 GB per vCPU to satisfy high memory footprint requirements. Memory subsystem tests show strong throughput, recording 506.7 GB/sec in large-block read operations and 207.77 GB/sec in large-block writes, both placing in the top 10 percent of benchmarks. For low-latency temporary data requirements, the VM bundles 5670 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. The configuration includes no discrete graphics processing units and zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark measurements indicate balanced multi-threaded compute and data handling capacity. The instance achieves a PassMark CPU score of 93,126.45 and a multi-core Geekbench score of 20,410.0, alongside strong performance in multi-threaded bzip3 decompression and Clang software compilation. In transactional tests, the system delivered 35,335.9 operations in PassMark database benchmarks and sustained 122.52 million operations per second in Redis SET tests. Static web serving reached 136.17 GB/sec throughput. In CPU-driven inference benchmarks, prompt processing reached 261.63 tokens per second on 7B parameter models.

The dense hardware allocation delivers qualitative cost efficiency for large-scale enterprise deployments requiring high concurrent thread counts alongside high RAM capacity, eliminating the need to cluster multiple smaller instances. Tradeoffs include average single-threaded compression and decompression rates, indicating that workloads limited by single-core speed do not benefit from this profile. Microsoft Azure E96ds_v6 is suited for large relational databases, in-memory caching tiers like Redis, enterprise ETL pipelines, and high-concurrency static web serving.
description: Microsoft Azure E96ds_v6 is a memory-optimized cloud server built on 96 dedicated vCPUs from an Intel Xeon 8573C processor clocking at 4.2 GHz across 48 physical cores. The instance pairs 768.0 GB of system RAM with 5670 GB of local NVMe SSD storage and includes support for AMX and AVX-512 extensions, while excluding discrete GPUs. In synthetic and practical benchmarks, the server registers top-tier results in uncached memory bandwidth, PassMark database operations, and static web serving throughput exceeding 136 GB/sec. Multi-threaded compute scores are strong across Geekbench, PassMark, and stress-ng suites, though single-threaded performance remains average. The resource allocation provides high resource density for scale-up systems, making the E96ds_v6 well fitted for large in-memory databases, distributed caching layers, enterprise data processing, and heavy analytical queries requiring extensive local storage scratch space.
